text:
meera: Quick sync — hosted embeddings roadmap for Q4. Need to decide: SLA targets (p95/p99), caching approach (prefix vs per-customer KV), and launch criteria for a public beta. Several customers are asking for low-latency single-vector calls (~50-80ms p95). @omar @liz can we hit that on current infra or do we need a special fast-path?

omar: 50-80ms p95 for single-embedding is... ambitious. For small batch=1 on A100/GPU-optimized nodes we can approach 80ms for smaller models (e.g., s-*, quantized), but not reliably at scale without a fast cache. Autoscaling also has cold-starts. Need a canary traffic pattern for burst tests.

liz: Agree with @omar. Two levers: 1) per-customer in-memory KV cache for hot vectors (fastest), 2) prefix/shared cache for repeated inputs (cheaper). Per-customer cache increases memory footprint but gives predictable p95. Also model choice: 1536-dim vs 768-dim — 768 will be faster/cost-effective but may reduce quality for some use cases.

alex: From infra side: we can expose a "fast-path" fleet of pinned instances (smaller models, pre-loaded weights, no multiplexing) to guarantee low p95. Tradeoff is cost + lower utilization. If we combine that with a small LRU in front for recent vectors we can serve most single-shot requests under 100ms.

sam: For public beta launch criteria proposal (first pass):
- SLO: p95 <= 120ms for single-embedding on fast-path for 95% of tenants during business-hours load.
- Availability: 99.9% for embedding endpoints.
- Cost target: <= $0.40 per 1k embeddings (768-dim) in common workload profiles.
- Quality: embedding cosine similarity regression < 3% vs baseline model on customer validation sets.
- Observability: per-tenant token/embedding latency dashboards, error-rate alerts, and perf regression alerting.

jordan: Customer asks: rerank + embeddings latency matters end-to-end. They're fine with 2 calls if total p95 < 200ms. We should include multi-call flow in acceptance tests. Also several enterprise customers will require private deploy compatibility.

eval-bot: Eval summary for candidate models (run: 2026-01-17):
- model-a-768: avg latency(1) 62ms, p95 110ms, quality delta 0.8%
- model-b-1536: avg latency(1) 120ms, p95 210ms, quality delta -0.5%
Link: https://redwood-internal/evals/2026/embeddings-jan17

meera: Helpful — propose we scope Q4 public beta as: fast-path fleet + per-tenant in-memory cache + default model=model-a-768, opt-in model-b-1536 for quality-sensitive tenants. Launch checklist:
- rollout policy (canary -> 25% -> 100%)
- perf regression suite (single-shot & rerank flows)
- cost monitoring and throttle policies
- doc + quickstart for opting into high-accuracy model

alex: Sample rollout config (canary rules):
```
rollout: {
  canary: 5%,
  stage2: 25% if p95_canary < 150ms and error_rate < 0.5%,
  full: 100% if stage2 conditions hold for 48h
}
```

omar: Also add chaos tests for node reboots and cache eviction. We saw cache warmup spikes last quarter. Add synthetic traffic that mimics 1:1 small QPS.

liz: Owner requests:
- fast-path infra: alex
- caching api + per-tenant memory limits: liz
- perf tests + infra automation: omar
- launch criteria + customer comms: meera + sam

meera: Cool. Assigning owners and will add to roadmap doc. Next steps: alex + liz to post perf/cost estimate by EOD Friday, @eval-bot to run rerank end-to-end tests and post results. If we all agree, I'll schedule a 30-min sync on Monday to finalize SLAs. :thumbsup:
